newsitem.title: THAILAND: Rebel groups urge ASEAN not to admit Burma yet.
newsitem.headline: Rebel groups urge ASEAN not to admit Burma yet.

text.p: Sixteen Burmese ethnic rebel groups on Wednesday urged the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to postpone acceptance of Burma into the grouping until it changed its political system.
A statement jointly issued by the groups, obtained by Reuters on Wednesday, said they supported opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi.
"We demand the postponement of the acceptance of Burma as a member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations until there is positive political change," it said.
Burma is seeking to gain full ASEAN membership along with Laos and Cambodia this year. ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
The statement also urged Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) to hold talks with the Nobel Peace laureate and the ethnic groups to discuss how to bring democracy to Burma.
The statement was issued following a week-long seminar of leaders of the groups at Mae Tha Raw Hta in eastern Burma.
The 16 groups that signed the resolution were members of the defunct Democratic Alliance of Burma.
Fourteen of the groups, including the United Wa State Army and the New Mon State Army, have signed peace agreements with the SLORC.
The predominantly-Christian Karen National Union (KNU) and a small guerrillas faction, the Karenni National Progress Party (KNPP), have not yet signed ceasefires and are still fighting for autonomy.
